abstract: Transition from cold limitation to drought limitation due to climate change is widespread in boreal forests. We explored in the scope of the Dry Boreal Forest Long-Term Nitrogen Fertilization Experiment (DryBoreal-LTNE) in southern boreal forests of Mongolia how N supply interacts with tree water and C relations in forests of Larix sibirica, which are naturally drought-limited. Using branches of mature L. sibirica subjected to N fertilization of 6.25-25 kg N ha-1 a-1, we conducted CO2/H2O gas exchange measurements to examine how N availability interferes with the climatic control of stomatal conductance (gs) in L. sibirica. We tested the hypotheses that gs increases with increasing N availability and that this increase can be translated into increased net photosynthesis (A) in L. sibirica even under the dry continental climate of Mongolia. We could confirm the first hypothesis and found that A decreased at low fertilization (6.25 kg N ha-1 a-1) probably caused by increases in respiration due to metabolic costs of intensified N uptake. A attained the highest values at 12.5 kg N ha-1 a-1, but declined at the highest fertilization level of 25 kg N ha-1 a-1. Our results demonstrate that research on the drought tolerance of boreal forests under climate change should not only focus on changes in temperature, vapor pressure deficit, and precipitation, but should take N availability into account, especially as N availability is thought to decrease in remote boreal forests due to elevated atmospheric CO2 concentrations and can be locally influenced by land use.
